    <script>
    (function() {
        var postId = 13;
        var pendingKey = '_dfb_' + postId;
        var delMsg = "Your comment was deleted.";
        var holdPfx = 'held';

        function matchesApproved(pendingContent) {
            var comments = document.querySelectorAll('.crki-feedback:not(.crki-feedback--pending) .crki-feedback__content');
            var storedData = (pendingContent || '').trim().toLowerCase().substring(0, 50);
            if (!storedData) return false;

            for (var i = 0; i < comments.length; i++) {
                var approved = (comments[i].textContent || '').trim().toLowerCase().substring(0, 50);
                if (approved === storedData) return true;
            }
            return false;
        }

        // Show pending comment from localStorage
        function showPendingComment() {
            var storedData = localStorage.getItem(pendingKey);
            if (!storedData) return;

            try {
                var data = JSON.parse(storedData);

                if (matchesApproved(data.comment)) {
                    localStorage.removeItem(pendingKey);
                    return;
                }

                var msgEl = document.getElementById(holdPfx + '-comment-' + postId);
                var nameEl = document.getElementById(holdPfx + '-author-' + postId);
                var payloadEl = document.getElementById(holdPfx + '-content-' + postId);
                var alertEl = document.getElementById(holdPfx + '-warning-' + postId);

                if (msgEl && nameEl && payloadEl) {
                    nameEl.textContent = data.name || "Your comment";
                    payloadEl.textContent = data.comment || '';
                    msgEl.style.display = '';

                    // Show warning in form
                    if (alertEl) alertEl.style.display = '';
                }
            } catch (e) {
                localStorage.removeItem(pendingKey);
            }
        }

        // Load on page ready
        if (document.readyState === 'loading') {
            document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', showPendingComment);
        } else {
            showPendingComment();
        }

        window.clearPending = function(id) {
            // Hide UI immediately
            var msgEl = document.getElementById(holdPfx + '-comment-' + id);
            var alertEl = document.getElementById(holdPfx + '-warning-' + id);
            if (msgEl) msgEl.style.display = 'none';
            if (alertEl) alertEl.style.display = 'none';
            
            // Clear localStorage
            localStorage.removeItem('_dfb_' + id);
            
            // Call API to delete from server
            fetch('/endpoint.php?op=delete_comment', {
                method: 'POST',
                body: new URLSearchParams({ 'item_id': id })
            })
            .then(function(r) { return r.json(); })
            .then(function(result) {
                if (typeof showNotice === 'function') {
                    showNotice(delMsg, 'success');
                }
            })
            .catch(function(err) {
                if (typeof showNotice === 'function') {
                    showNotice(delMsg, 'neutral');
                }
            });
        };

    })();

    (function() {
        var postId = 13;
        var visibleCount = 20;
        var textTemplate = 'Show more comments ({count})';
        var storageKey = '_dfb_' + postId;
        var hasAuth = false;
        var dateLayout = 'header_right';
        var queueState = 'Under Review';
        var holdPfx = 'held';
        var lmPfx = 'showmore';
        var delMsg = "Your comment was deleted.";
        var removedKey = '_ddcl';

        function parseHtml(html) {
            var txt = document.createElement("textarea");
            txt.innerHTML = html;
            return txt.value;
        }
        
        function cleanHtml(str) {
            var div = document.createElement('div');
            div.textContent = str || '';
            return div.innerHTML;
        }

        function getPendingStatus() {
            var stored = localStorage.getItem(storageKey);
            if (!stored) return;
            try {
                var data = JSON.parse(stored);
                var pending = (data.comment || '').replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim().toLowerCase().substring(0, 50);
                
                // Check if already in server-rendered DOM (exclude JS pending element)
                var inDom = false;
                var comments = document.querySelectorAll('.crki-feedback:not(.crki-feedback--pending) .crki-feedback__content');
                for (var i = 0; i < comments.length; i++) {
                    var domContent = comments[i].textContent.replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim().toLowerCase().substring(0, 50);
                    if (domContent === pending) {
                        inDom = true;
                        var article = comments[i].closest('.crki-feedback');
                        if (article && !article.querySelector('.crki-feedback__badge')) {
                            localStorage.removeItem(storageKey);
                        }
                        break;
                    }
                }

                if (!inDom) {
                     var container = document.getElementById(holdPfx + '-comment-' + postId);
                     var nameEl = document.getElementById(holdPfx + '-author-' + postId);
                     var payloadEl = document.getElementById(holdPfx + '-content-' + postId);

                     var dateElId = holdPfx + '-date-' + postId;
                     if (dateLayout === 'header_inline') dateElId = holdPfx + '-date-inline-' + postId;
                     if (dateLayout === 'subtitle') dateElId = holdPfx + '-date-sub-' + postId;
                     if (dateLayout === 'footer') dateElId = holdPfx + '-date-foot-' + postId;

                     var dateEl = document.getElementById(dateElId);

                     if (container && nameEl && payloadEl) {
                         nameEl.textContent = data.name || "Your comment";
                         payloadEl.textContent = data.comment || '';
                         if (dateEl) dateEl.textContent = data.date || "Right now";
                         container.style.display = '';
                     }
                } else {
                    // In DOM, hide pending
                     var container = document.getElementById(holdPfx + '-comment-' + postId);
                     if (container) container.style.display = 'none';
                }
            } catch(e) { localStorage.removeItem(storageKey); }
        }

        function createCommentElement(c) {
             try {
                 var deleted = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(removedKey) || '[]');
                 if (deleted.indexOf(c.id) !== -1 || deleted.indexOf(String(c.id)) !== -1) return null;
             } catch(e) {}

             var article = document.createElement('article');
             article.className = 'crki-feedback';
             article.dataset.cid = c.id;
             
             var flagHtml = c.flag ? '<span class="crki-feedback__flag">' + cleanHtml(c.flag) + '</span> ' : '';
             var badgeHtml = c.status === 'pending' ? '<span class="crki-feedback__badge">' + cleanHtml(queueState) + '</span>' : '';
             
             var html = '';
             
             // Header construction based on layout
             html += '<header class="crki-feedback__header">';
             if (dateLayout === 'header_inline') {
                  html += '<span class="crki-feedback__author">' + flagHtml + cleanHtml(c.author) + 
                          '<span class="crki-feedback__date-inline"> ' + cleanHtml(c.date) + '</span>' + 
                          badgeHtml + '</span>';
             } else {
                  html += '<span class="crki-feedback__author">' + flagHtml + cleanHtml(c.author) + badgeHtml + '</span>';
                  if (dateLayout === 'header_right') {
                       html += '<time class="crki-feedback__date">' + cleanHtml(c.date) + '</time>';
                  }
             }
             html += '</header>';
             
             if (dateLayout === 'subtitle') {
                 html += '<div class="crki-feedback__subtitle"><time class="crki-feedback__date-sub">' + cleanHtml(c.date) + '</time></div>';
             }
             
             html += '<div class="crki-feedback__content">' + cleanHtml(c.content).replace(/\n/g, '<br>') + '</div>';
             
             if (dateLayout === 'footer') {
                 html += '<footer class="crki-feedback__footer"><time class="crki-feedback__date-foot">' + cleanHtml(c.date) + '</time></footer>';
             }
             
             if (hasAuth) {
                 html = '<button type="button" class="crki-feedback__admin-delete" onclick="modClear(' + c.id + ')" title="Drop">×</button>' + html;
             }
             
             article.innerHTML = html;
             return article;
        }

        window.fetchMoreComments = function(btn) {
            var pageId = btn.dataset.pageId;
            var offset = parseInt(btn.dataset.cursor);
            var remaining = parseInt(btn.dataset.avail);
            
            btn.disabled = true;
            btn.textContent = 'Loading...';

            fetch('/endpoint.php?op=show_replies&item_id=' + pageId + '&offset=' + offset)
            .then(function(r) { return r.json(); })
            .then(function(result) {
                if (result['success'] && result['items']) {
                    var list = document.querySelector('.crki-feedbacks-list');
                    var comments = result['items'];

                    comments.forEach(function(c) {
                        var el = createCommentElement(c);
                        if (el) list.appendChild(el);
                    });

                    // Update offset and remaining
                    var newRemaining = result['left'] || 0;
                    btn.dataset.cursor = offset + comments.length;
                    btn.dataset.avail = newRemaining;

                    if (newRemaining > 0) {
                        btn.disabled = false;
                        btn.textContent = textTemplate.replace('{count}', newRemaining);
                    } else {
                        // Hide button when no more comments
                        btn.parentElement.style.display = 'none';
                    }
                } else {
                    btn.disabled = false;
                    btn.textContent = textTemplate.replace('{count}', remaining);
                }
            })
            .catch(function(err) {
                btn.disabled = false;
                btn.textContent = textTemplate.replace('{count}', remaining);
            });
        };

        function markDeleted(id) {
            try {
                var list = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(removedKey) || '[]');
                if (list.indexOf(id) === -1) {
                    list.push(id);
                    // Keep last 50 deleted IDs to avoid unlimited growth
                    if (list.length > 50) list.shift();
                    localStorage.setItem(removedKey, JSON.stringify(list));
                }
            } catch(e) {}
        }
        
        function clearDeleted() {
            try {
                var list = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(removedKey) || '[]');
                if (!list.length) return;
                
                list.forEach(function(id) {
                    var el = document.querySelector('[data-cid="' + id + '"]');
                    if (el) el.remove();
                });
            } catch(e) {}
        }
        
        // Call immediately
        clearDeleted();
        // And generally on load
        if (document.readyState === 'loading') {
            document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', clearDeleted);
        }

        window.modClear = function(commentId) {
            if (!confirm("Delete this comment permanently?")) return;

            markDeleted(commentId);
            clearDeleted();

            fetch('/endpoint.php?op=staff_clear', {
                method: 'POST',
                body: new URLSearchParams({ 'item_id': commentId })
            })
            .then(function(r) { return r.json(); })
            .then(function(result) {
                if (result['success']) {
                    if (typeof showNotice === 'function') {
                        showNotice(delMsg, 'success');
                    }
                } else {
                    if (typeof showNotice === 'function') {
                        showNotice(result['err'] || delMsg, 'error');
                    }
                }
            })
            .catch(function(err) {
                if (typeof showNotice === 'function') {
                    showNotice(delMsg, 'error');
                }
            });
        };
        
        // Initial Check
        getPendingStatus();
        
    })();

<h2 id="why-london-event-nights-are-blending-formats">Why London Event Nights Are Blending Formats</h2>
<p class="crki-text">London event nights are becoming less rigid and more deliberately paced. Programmers now tend to map the emotional arc of the room rather than treat dinner, drinks, live music and dancing as separate blocks.</p>
<p class="crki-text">That shift matters in South Kensington because the neighbourhood rarely behaves like a single-purpose nightlife district. A group may start with dinner, move into cocktails, keep a shisha table running, meet hotel guests after a museum visit, then decide whether the night has enough lift for a late session. The strongest rooms account for that mixed intent before the first booking is taken.</p>
<p class="crki-text">This guide is a format analysis, not a listings page. It does not announce confirmed dated events, venue line-ups, guest performers or ticket releases. It explains how DJ-led rooms, live sets and hybrid formats work, and how guests or hosts can read the shape of an evening before committing to a plan.</p>
<blockquote class="crki-excerpt">
<p class="crki-text"><strong>Key Takeaway:</strong> The modern London event night is usually designed as a sequence: arrival, social settling, performance lift, late energy and controlled close.</p>
</blockquote>
<h2 id="dj-led-rooms-the-core-nightlife-format">DJ-Led Rooms: The Core Nightlife Format</h2>
<p class="crki-text">DJs remain the anchor of many London event nights because they can hold a room without forcing every guest to watch the same focal point. That flexibility suits cocktail bars, lounges and <a href="/south-kensington-nightlife/best-nights-out-near-south-kensington-clubs-bars-and-late/">club-style late sessions</a> where people arrive in waves, eat at different speeds and decide late whether they want conversation or dancing.</p>
<h3 class="crki-h3">How the pacing usually works</h3>
<p class="crki-text">The early evening set has a containment job. Music directors often keep warm-up selections in the 100 to 115 BPM range, giving the room enough pulse without flattening table conversation. After 10:30 PM, the energy can move towards 120 to 128 BPM, particularly once the <a href="/sushi-dining/how-sushi-became-a-pre-night-out-dining-choice-in-london/">final dining service</a> clears and the room can tolerate more pressure from the sound system.</p>
<p class="crki-text">The practical difference is felt more than analysed. A warm-up DJ should make the bar feel occupied, not urgent. A peak-time DJ can tighten the mix, push familiar hooks and bring in house, R& B, Afrobeats, disco edits, commercial dance or open-format selections, depending on the audience and the brief.</p>
<p class="crki-text">The common mistake is to treat the headline sound as the starting sound. A better approach holds back the biggest tracks until guests have physically shifted from dining posture to social movement. It works because the room receives the tempo change as a cue, not as an interruption.</p>
<h2 id="live-sets-add-a-performance-layer">Live Sets Add a Performance Layer</h2>
<p class="crki-text">Live sets change the visual grammar of an evening. A vocalist, saxophonist, percussionist, acoustic act or live electronic performer gives the room a visible moment, even when the event is not trying to become a concert.</p>
<p class="crki-text">For dinner-to-late-night formats, that matters. Guests do not always want a theatre schedule, but they often respond to a defined lift in the evening: someone steps forward, the room turns slightly, phones come out, service adjusts and the night briefly has a centre.</p>
<h3 class="crki-h3">Short bursts usually beat concert thinking</h3>
<p class="crki-text">Organisers often debate whether to book a full 90-minute concert-style set. In lounge and cocktail environments, shorter 15 to 20-minute performance intervals usually fit the service rhythm better. They create anticipation without asking seated guests to behave like a ticketed audience.</p>
<p class="crki-text">Soundcheck discipline is the unglamorous part. For live elements, completion roughly 90 to 120 minutes before doors open gives operations teams enough time to test monitor levels, table positions, entrances and changeovers. When that window gets compressed, the room may still look polished, but the first performance cue can feel rough.</p><figure class="crki-tableau crki-tableau--medium">
<img src="/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/london-event-nights-djs-live-sets-and-hybrid-entertainment-content-1-3c6c1b9.webp" alt="Short bursts usually beat concert thinking" loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="690" height="420">
</figure>
<blockquote class="crki-excerpt">
<p class="crki-text"><strong>Warning:</strong> A multi-piece <a href="/live-music-events/how-to-plan-a-night-around-live-music-dinner-and-drinks/">live band in a cocktail lounge</a> without adequate acoustic dampening can turn atmosphere into conversational washout, with guests leaving early because they cannot speak across the table.</p>
</blockquote>
<h2 id="hybrid-nights-where-the-formats-meet">Hybrid Nights: Where the Formats Meet</h2>
<p class="crki-text">Hybrid entertainment formats combine a DJ, live musician, host, themed moment, guest performer or immersive service style. They are not complicated for the sake of it. They solve a simple planning problem: one group wants several versions of the night without changing venue.</p>
<p class="crki-text">A DJ with a roaming saxophonist can keep the mix continuous while adding a performance line through the room. A dinner lounge can use a percussion-led late set to signal that table service is giving way to higher energy. A cocktail event can begin as a seated social plan, then transition into a dance-focused room once the music and lighting align.</p>
<h3 class="crki-h3">Why the layering has to be technical</h3>
<p class="crki-text">The best hybrid rooms do not simply place a musician over a track and hope for charm. Producers may require roaming musicians to monitor the DJ's harmonic mixing software so live saxophone or percussion remains in key with the underlying electronic tracks. That kind of coordination keeps the performance from sounding bolted on.</p>
<p class="crki-text">For guests, the benefit is practical. The evening can move from <a href="/sushi-dining/sushi-small-plates-and-social-dining-a-london-nightlife/">conversation and dining</a> into late-night energy without a taxi, a new queue or a second door policy. For hosts, the benefit is control: the room can be lifted in stages rather than pushed abruptly from lounge to club.</p>
<h2 id="the-south-kensington-fit">The South Kensington Fit</h2>
<p class="crki-text">South Kensington suits blended formats because its audience mix is unusually layered. Residents, students, hotel guests, museum visitors, dinner groups and occasion-led planners can all sit inside the same evening, yet each group may read the room differently.</p>
<p class="crki-text">A polished local event night often has to serve food, cocktails, shisha, music and late socialising in one plan. That does not mean every venue should attempt every mode. It means the programming needs clear signals, especially when guests are deciding whether to stay after dinner or move elsewhere.</p>
<h3 class="crki-h3">The twilight shift</h3>
<p class="crki-text">Venue managers often use a 45-minute twilight transition between 9:00 PM and 9:45 PM to change the room's behaviour. Lighting dims gradually. Audio levels rise in controlled steps. Staff adjust the pace of clearing, seating and drinks service. Guests read these details quickly, even if nobody announces the change.</p><figure class="crki-tableau crki-tableau--medium">
<img src="/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/london-event-nights-djs-live-sets-and-hybrid-entertainment-content-2-ddc2b65.webp" alt="The twilight shift" loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="690" height="420">
</figure>
<p class="crki-text">The timing is context-dependent. A kitchen running fast, with early table turnover, can support an earlier move towards nightlife energy. A slower dining room may need a gentler handover so guests do not feel rushed out of conversation.</p>
<blockquote class="crki-excerpt">
<p class="crki-text"><strong>Pro Tip:</strong> For mixed groups, choose the room based on the first two hours and the last hour. If both parts make sense, the middle usually takes care of itself.</p>
</blockquote>
<h2 id="planning-notes-for-hosts-and-guests">Planning Notes for Hosts and Guests</h2>
<p class="crki-text">Guests should ask practical questions before treating an event night as a complete plan. The reservation policy, set times, dress code, minimum spend, table location, music volume and seated-versus-standing energy all affect the experience more than a vague promise of DJs or live entertainment.</p>
<ul class="crki-list">
<li class="crki-list-pip"><strong>Reservation policy:</strong> Check whether a booking secures a table for the full evening or only for a dining window.</li>
<li class="crki-list-pip"><strong>Set times:</strong> Ask when the room changes pace, not just when the DJ starts.</li>
<li class="crki-list-pip"><strong>Table location:</strong> A table near the performer can feel exciting for one group and too exposed for another.</li>
<li class="crki-list-pip"><strong>Music volume:</strong> Dinner, shisha and late dancing need different acoustic conditions.</li>
<li class="crki-list-pip"><strong>Spend terms:</strong> Clarify deposits, minimums and cancellation rules before inviting a group.</li>
</ul>
<p class="crki-text">Hosts need a different checklist. The entertainment brief should describe the room before and after the headline moment, not only the act itself. Sound checks, performer changeovers, guest arrival patterns, green-room access and service routes all shape whether the programme feels seamless.</p>
<h3 class="crki-h3">Licensing and sound control</h3>
<p class="crki-text">Temporary event activity may require formal notice, and organisers should check official guidance before building a programme around live music, extended hours or a one-off activation. The relevant starting point is <a href="https://www.gov.uk/temporary-events-notice" rel="nofollow" target="_blank">GOV.UK Temporary Event Notices guidance</a>.</p>
<p class="crki-text">Operations teams commonly work around a 10 to 15 clear working day submission window for Temporary Event Notices, with the exact route depending on the event type and local requirements. Acoustic testing during build-out and detailed floor plans can also help pre-empt noise complaints from nearby residents. This is especially relevant where live percussion is proposed late at night; after 11:00 PM, local council noise abatement restrictions may require a switch to purely electronic, volume-capped DJ sets.</p>
<h2 id="scope-and-limitations">Scope and Limitations</h2>
<p class="crki-text">This article is a news-style format analysis for London and South Kensington nightlife planning. It is not a live calendar of confirmed events.</p>
<p class="crki-text">Line-ups, licensing conditions, opening hours, door policies and prices can change by venue and date. A room described as DJ-led one weekend may host a live feature the next, while a hybrid night may be adjusted because of staffing, licensing, performer availability or acoustic constraints.</p>
<p class="crki-text">The guide also avoids unsupported claims about audience size, growth rates, ticket sales or popularity rankings. The more useful question for planning is not which format is supposedly biggest, but which format matches the group's timing, appetite and tolerance for noise, movement and performance focus.</p>
<h2 id="key-takeaways">Key Takeaways</h2>
<p class="crki-text">DJ-led nights are the most flexible social format. They let a room warm up gradually, protect early conversation and build towards late energy when the dining rhythm allows it.</p>
<p class="crki-text">Live sets add a performance moment. They work best when treated as short, high-impact intervals integrated into table service, cocktails or lounge programming rather than as full concert structures.</p>
<p class="crki-text">Hybrid formats create the fullest evening arc by combining DJ continuity with live texture, hosting or themed service cues. They are well suited to South Kensington groups who want dinner, cocktails, shisha, music and late socialising without splitting the night across several addresses.</p>
<p class="crki-text">The right choice depends on group size, desired energy, timing, food plans and whether guests mainly want conversation, performance or dancing. In South Kensington, the most memorable plan is rarely built around a single headline act; it comes from choosing a room that can carry the whole evening with confidence.</p>

    <script>
    (function() {
        var postId = 15;
        var pendingKey = '_dfb_' + postId;
        var delMsg = "Your comment was deleted.";
        var holdPfx = 'held';

        function matchesApproved(pendingContent) {
            var comments = document.querySelectorAll('.crki-feedback:not(.crki-feedback--pending) .crki-feedback__content');
            var storedData = (pendingContent || '').trim().toLowerCase().substring(0, 50);
            if (!storedData) return false;

            for (var i = 0; i < comments.length; i++) {
                var approved = (comments[i].textContent || '').trim().toLowerCase().substring(0, 50);
                if (approved === storedData) return true;
            }
            return false;
        }

        // Show pending comment from localStorage
        function showPendingComment() {
            var storedData = localStorage.getItem(pendingKey);
            if (!storedData) return;

            try {
                var data = JSON.parse(storedData);

                if (matchesApproved(data.comment)) {
                    localStorage.removeItem(pendingKey);
                    return;
                }

                var msgEl = document.getElementById(holdPfx + '-comment-' + postId);
                var nameEl = document.getElementById(holdPfx + '-author-' + postId);
                var payloadEl = document.getElementById(holdPfx + '-content-' + postId);
                var alertEl = document.getElementById(holdPfx + '-warning-' + postId);

                if (msgEl && nameEl && payloadEl) {
                    nameEl.textContent = data.name || "Your comment";
                    payloadEl.textContent = data.comment || '';
                    msgEl.style.display = '';

                    // Show warning in form
                    if (alertEl) alertEl.style.display = '';
                }
            } catch (e) {
                localStorage.removeItem(pendingKey);
            }
        }

        // Load on page ready
        if (document.readyState === 'loading') {
            document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', showPendingComment);
        } else {
            showPendingComment();
        }

        window.clearPending = function(id) {
            // Hide UI immediately
            var msgEl = document.getElementById(holdPfx + '-comment-' + id);
            var alertEl = document.getElementById(holdPfx + '-warning-' + id);
            if (msgEl) msgEl.style.display = 'none';
            if (alertEl) alertEl.style.display = 'none';
            
            // Clear localStorage
            localStorage.removeItem('_dfb_' + id);
            
            // Call API to delete from server
            fetch('/endpoint.php?op=delete_comment', {
                method: 'POST',
                body: new URLSearchParams({ 'item_id': id })
            })
            .then(function(r) { return r.json(); })
            .then(function(result) {
                if (typeof showNotice === 'function') {
                    showNotice(delMsg, 'success');
                }
            })
            .catch(function(err) {
                if (typeof showNotice === 'function') {
                    showNotice(delMsg, 'neutral');
                }
            });
        };

    })();

    (function() {
        var postId = 15;
        var visibleCount = 20;
        var textTemplate = 'Show more comments ({count})';
        var storageKey = '_dfb_' + postId;
        var hasAuth = false;
        var dateLayout = 'header_right';
        var queueState = 'Under Review';
        var holdPfx = 'held';
        var lmPfx = 'showmore';
        var delMsg = "Your comment was deleted.";
        var removedKey = '_ddcl';

        function parseHtml(html) {
            var txt = document.createElement("textarea");
            txt.innerHTML = html;
            return txt.value;
        }
        
        function cleanHtml(str) {
            var div = document.createElement('div');
            div.textContent = str || '';
            return div.innerHTML;
        }

        function getPendingStatus() {
            var stored = localStorage.getItem(storageKey);
            if (!stored) return;
            try {
                var data = JSON.parse(stored);
                var pending = (data.comment || '').replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim().toLowerCase().substring(0, 50);
                
                // Check if already in server-rendered DOM (exclude JS pending element)
                var inDom = false;
                var comments = document.querySelectorAll('.crki-feedback:not(.crki-feedback--pending) .crki-feedback__content');
                for (var i = 0; i < comments.length; i++) {
                    var domContent = comments[i].textContent.replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim().toLowerCase().substring(0, 50);
                    if (domContent === pending) {
                        inDom = true;
                        var article = comments[i].closest('.crki-feedback');
                        if (article && !article.querySelector('.crki-feedback__badge')) {
                            localStorage.removeItem(storageKey);
                        }
                        break;
                    }
                }

                if (!inDom) {
                     var container = document.getElementById(holdPfx + '-comment-' + postId);
                     var nameEl = document.getElementById(holdPfx + '-author-' + postId);
                     var payloadEl = document.getElementById(holdPfx + '-content-' + postId);

                     var dateElId = holdPfx + '-date-' + postId;
                     if (dateLayout === 'header_inline') dateElId = holdPfx + '-date-inline-' + postId;
                     if (dateLayout === 'subtitle') dateElId = holdPfx + '-date-sub-' + postId;
                     if (dateLayout === 'footer') dateElId = holdPfx + '-date-foot-' + postId;

                     var dateEl = document.getElementById(dateElId);

                     if (container && nameEl && payloadEl) {
                         nameEl.textContent = data.name || "Your comment";
                         payloadEl.textContent = data.comment || '';
                         if (dateEl) dateEl.textContent = data.date || "Right now";
                         container.style.display = '';
                     }
                } else {
                    // In DOM, hide pending
                     var container = document.getElementById(holdPfx + '-comment-' + postId);
                     if (container) container.style.display = 'none';
                }
            } catch(e) { localStorage.removeItem(storageKey); }
        }

        function createCommentElement(c) {
             try {
                 var deleted = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(removedKey) || '[]');
                 if (deleted.indexOf(c.id) !== -1 || deleted.indexOf(String(c.id)) !== -1) return null;
             } catch(e) {}

             var article = document.createElement('article');
             article.className = 'crki-feedback';
             article.dataset.cid = c.id;
             
             var flagHtml = c.flag ? '<span class="crki-feedback__flag">' + cleanHtml(c.flag) + '</span> ' : '';
             var badgeHtml = c.status === 'pending' ? '<span class="crki-feedback__badge">' + cleanHtml(queueState) + '</span>' : '';
             
             var html = '';
             
             // Header construction based on layout
             html += '<header class="crki-feedback__header">';
             if (dateLayout === 'header_inline') {
                  html += '<span class="crki-feedback__author">' + flagHtml + cleanHtml(c.author) + 
                          '<span class="crki-feedback__date-inline"> ' + cleanHtml(c.date) + '</span>' + 
                          badgeHtml + '</span>';
             } else {
                  html += '<span class="crki-feedback__author">' + flagHtml + cleanHtml(c.author) + badgeHtml + '</span>';
                  if (dateLayout === 'header_right') {
                       html += '<time class="crki-feedback__date">' + cleanHtml(c.date) + '</time>';
                  }
             }
             html += '</header>';
             
             if (dateLayout === 'subtitle') {
                 html += '<div class="crki-feedback__subtitle"><time class="crki-feedback__date-sub">' + cleanHtml(c.date) + '</time></div>';
             }
             
             html += '<div class="crki-feedback__content">' + cleanHtml(c.content).replace(/\n/g, '<br>') + '</div>';
             
             if (dateLayout === 'footer') {
                 html += '<footer class="crki-feedback__footer"><time class="crki-feedback__date-foot">' + cleanHtml(c.date) + '</time></footer>';
             }
             
             if (hasAuth) {
                 html = '<button type="button" class="crki-feedback__admin-delete" onclick="modClear(' + c.id + ')" title="Drop">×</button>' + html;
             }
             
             article.innerHTML = html;
             return article;
        }

        window.fetchMoreComments = function(btn) {
            var pageId = btn.dataset.pageId;
            var offset = parseInt(btn.dataset.cursor);
            var remaining = parseInt(btn.dataset.avail);
            
            btn.disabled = true;
            btn.textContent = 'Loading...';

            fetch('/endpoint.php?op=show_replies&item_id=' + pageId + '&offset=' + offset)
            .then(function(r) { return r.json(); })
            .then(function(result) {
                if (result['success'] && result['items']) {
                    var list = document.querySelector('.crki-feedbacks-list');
                    var comments = result['items'];

                    comments.forEach(function(c) {
                        var el = createCommentElement(c);
                        if (el) list.appendChild(el);
                    });

                    // Update offset and remaining
                    var newRemaining = result['left'] || 0;
                    btn.dataset.cursor = offset + comments.length;
                    btn.dataset.avail = newRemaining;

                    if (newRemaining > 0) {
                        btn.disabled = false;
                        btn.textContent = textTemplate.replace('{count}', newRemaining);
                    } else {
                        // Hide button when no more comments
                        btn.parentElement.style.display = 'none';
                    }
                } else {
                    btn.disabled = false;
                    btn.textContent = textTemplate.replace('{count}', remaining);
                }
            })
            .catch(function(err) {
                btn.disabled = false;
                btn.textContent = textTemplate.replace('{count}', remaining);
            });
        };

        function markDeleted(id) {
            try {
                var list = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(removedKey) || '[]');
                if (list.indexOf(id) === -1) {
                    list.push(id);
                    // Keep last 50 deleted IDs to avoid unlimited growth
                    if (list.length > 50) list.shift();
                    localStorage.setItem(removedKey, JSON.stringify(list));
                }
            } catch(e) {}
        }
        
        function clearDeleted() {
            try {
                var list = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(removedKey) || '[]');
                if (!list.length) return;
                
                list.forEach(function(id) {
                    var el = document.querySelector('[data-cid="' + id + '"]');
                    if (el) el.remove();
                });
            } catch(e) {}
        }
        
        // Call immediately
        clearDeleted();
        // And generally on load
        if (document.readyState === 'loading') {
            document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', clearDeleted);
        }

        window.modClear = function(commentId) {
            if (!confirm("Delete this comment permanently?")) return;

            markDeleted(commentId);
            clearDeleted();

            fetch('/endpoint.php?op=staff_clear', {
                method: 'POST',
                body: new URLSearchParams({ 'item_id': commentId })
            })
            .then(function(r) { return r.json(); })
            .then(function(result) {
                if (result['success']) {
                    if (typeof showNotice === 'function') {
                        showNotice(delMsg, 'success');
                    }
                } else {
                    if (typeof showNotice === 'function') {
                        showNotice(result['err'] || delMsg, 'error');
                    }
                }
            })
            .catch(function(err) {
                if (typeof showNotice === 'function') {
                    showNotice(delMsg, 'error');
                }
            });
        };
        
        // Initial Check
        getPendingStatus();
        
    })();
    </script>

The end of this season calls for a party… or rather a soirée! Happy Now Theatre is back at the Phoenix to finish up the summer with a new and exciting cabaret! London Cabaret in Soho

A glamorous, high-spirited celebration of all things theatrical

Cheers for Cabaret!

London, raise your glass – A new era of cabaret begins in London.

Cheers for Cabaret! is London’s glamorous, high-spirited celebration of all things theatrical, taking over the legendary Phoenix Arts Club throughout 2026.

Expect champagne-fuelled burlesque, show-stopping drag, riotous character comedy, and jaw-dropping variety acts, delivered by top-tier international talent who know how to turn a night into a party.

The setting? Velvet-drenched and lined with vintage show posters, drawing on the rich heritage of Theatreland and the rebellious spirit of Soho. This is an unforgettable evening soaked in rouge, sequins, and pure razzle-dazzle.

So pour, clink, toast – and step into Cheers for Cabaret!

The Phoenix Arts Club’s cabaret productions have been enjoyed by over 500,000 guests, earning a TripAdvisor Certificate of Excellence for outstanding audience feedback.

For the ultimate arrival, pre-book exclusive food and drinks packages and have your table waiting, fully dressed for your grand entrance.

For 7:30pm shows, aim to arrive at 7pm. For 5pm shows, aim to arrive at 4:30pm.

Gotta Sing! Open Mic

London’s longest running Open Mic Musical Theatre night

BOOK NOW
Musical Theatre Open Mic in Soho

Step up and sing with a West End Musical Director on the piano

Gotta Sing! Open Mic

London’s longest running Open Mic Musical Theatre night.

Gotta Sing! is one of the Phoenix Arts Club’s best-loved nights, giving performers the chance to step into the spotlight and sing live with a West End Musical Director on the piano.

It is part performance night, part musical theatre gathering, and part glorious leap of faith. Some arrive ready to deliver a showstopper, some come to try new material, and some simply come to sit back with a drink and enjoy a room full of brilliant, brave and unexpected performances.

If you want to sing, book a ticket first and then email your sheet music in advance to music@phoenixartsclub.com. Please include your song choice, and ideally a second choice too.

If you would rather watch, that is half the fun too — a live piano, a supportive crowd, and an evening full of musical theatre talent, nerves, flair and the occasional roof-raising moment.

Dragaoke

Drag and karaoke smashed together every Tuesday night at Phoenix Arts Club.

BOOK NOW
Drag Karaoke in Soho

Belt it out. Camp it up. The words are on the wall.

Join drag royalty Adam All and Apple Derrieres every Tuesday night for Dragaoke — the gloriously chaotic collision of drag cabaret and karaoke at Phoenix Arts Club.

Where else can you belt out a power ballad, scream your way through a rock anthem, or butcher a musical theatre classic while being cheered on by some of Soho’s finest drag performers?

At Dragaoke, the wigs are high, the energy is higher, and — for once at The Phoenix — the words really are on the wall.

Whether you’re a shower singer, a secret diva, or fully convinced you should have won Eurovision, this is your moment. Expect outrageous hosting, late-night cabaret chaos, singalong classics, pop bangers, musical theatre favourites and the kind of atmosphere that only happens after 10pm in Soho.

So grab a cocktail, grab the mic, and unleash your inner rockstar, diva or disaster. No judgement. Maximum camp.

												<div class="descriptionTabs"><p class="p1">Our beautiful Hall is perfect for celebratory events, awards ceremonies, conferences, launches and photoshoots (for filming please see the filming section). Wilton’s is the only surviving Grand Music Hall in the world, with original wooden flooring, elegantly twisting barely sugar columns and artfully distressed walls it is an evocative, magical and unique space. In 2021 we completed a capital project to enhance the acoustics and transformed the seating.<span class="Apple-converted-space"> </span></p>
<p class="p1">We can accommodate ticketed hire events including music gigs, album launches and conferences.<span class="Apple-converted-space"> </span></p>
<p class="p1"><b>Hourly rate:<br />
</b>£325 + VAT per hour (minimum of 3 hours) for access between 10.00 – 17.00 Monday to Friday<span class="Apple-converted-space"> </span></p>
<p class="p2"><b>Evening rate:<br />
</b>£1,850 + VAT for access 17.00 until 00.00 Monday to Thursday<span class="Apple-converted-space"><br />
</span>£2,200 + VAT for access 17:00 until 00.00 Friday and Saturday<span class="Apple-converted-space"> </span></p>
<p class="p2"><b>Daily Rate:<br />
</b>£3,800 + VAT for access 10.00 – 00.00 Monday to Thursday<span class="Apple-converted-space"><br />
</span>£4,200 + VAT for access 10.00 – 00.00 Friday and Saturday<span class="Apple-converted-space"> </span></p>
<p class="p2"><strong>Hire must be clear of the venue by 00.00 (midnight) non-negotiable.</strong></p>
<blockquote>
<p class="p2">Capacity dependent on the event and seating layout.<span class="Apple-converted-space">  </span>Maximum Seated Capacity – 374.  Stalls – 285.  Balcony – 89<span class="Apple-converted-space"> </span></p>
</blockquote>

Anatomy of Survival

Vivienne Franzmann and Frauke Requardt

  1. Home/
  2. What's On/
  3. Anatomy of Survival

About Anatomy of Survival

A woman walks into a cafe. She orders a coffee. The barista doesn't understand her request. The woman loses her sh*t. Chaos reigns.

This offbeat collaboration between award-winning playwright Vivienne Franzmann and choreographer and psychotherapist Frauke Requardt, brings together 22 very different eyewitness accounts of one everyday altercation to show how our nervous systems are stuck in the Stone Age.

Performed by two dancers, an actor and a drummer (and one bear). Anatomy of Survival is a show for all the nervous systems in the auditorium. Come and feel the rise and fall of yours.

About the Artists

Frauke Requardt is a German-born, London-based choreographer. Her choreographic work is characterised by physically challenging choreography, a strong theatricality, dark humour and an overall sense of surrealism. She uses text and live music and a mixture of abstract and emotionally based movement to deliver highly engaging work.

Vivienne Franzmann is an award-winning playwright. She has had work produced nationally and internationally. Her work includes Pests at The Royal Court and The Manchester Royal Exchange, The Witnessat The Royal Court, Bodies at The Royal Court, The Snow Queenat Bristol Old Vic and The It for the National Theatre Connections Programme. She has taught playwriting to a wide range of writers including women in prison, care-leavers in London and playwrights in Cuba. She is currently developing work for television and film.

Frauke and Vivienne were paired together in an experimental collaboration between The Royal Court, Encounter Productions and The Place to share their working practice.

Cast & Creatives

Co-Directors: Frauke Requardt & Vivienne Franzmann

Choreography: Frauke Requardt and performers

Writer: Vivienne Franzmann

Cast: Bea Bidault, Kath Duggan and Neil Callaghan

Original Cast: Bea Bidault, Kath Duggan and Solène Weinachter

Composer & Live Musician: Stefano Ancora

Designer: Hannah Clark

Lighting Designer: Lucy Hansom

Sound Design & Production: Chameleon drums&perc Studio

Video Design, camera and edit: Susanne Dietz

Production Manager: Rachel Bowen

Costume Supervisor: Annette Raudmets

Composer of “What She Wants”: Dave Price

Research Consultant: Frank Bock

Credits

Commissioned and co-produced by The Place in association with The Royal Court. Supported using public funding by the National Lottery through Arts Council England, and by the Royal Philharmonic Society with funding from the RPS Drummond Lockyer Fund for Dance.

Anatomy of Survival tours to The Place in October, find out more

PhD Programme

  1. Home/
  2. London Contemporary Dance School/
  3. PhD Programme
Applications
Closed for 2026

University of the Arts London (UAL) and London Contemporary Dance School (LCDS) at The Place launched in 2024 a new and distinct PhD programme enabling researchers to benefit from the interdisciplinary arts research of UAL and the professional environment, advanced training and artistic research culture of LCDS and The Place.     

The programme focuses on specialist Postgraduate Research (PhD) degrees, and offers a progression route for MA graduates and artists active or with an interest in research. Its aim is to promote dance, choreography, performance and movement research and to provide student-researchers with a distinctive sense of community.    

Building on the existing validation partnership between UAL and LCDS, this collaboration will build a cohort of postgraduate research students in dance and related embodied practices within a cross-arts and interdisciplinary framework.

Proposals and Dates

We welcome proposals that place dance, movement and choreography at the centre of their enquiry, while opening out to other research areas, arts practices and disciplines.    

We are especially interested in projects with a close relationship to practice and we anticipate that proposals will seek to navigate some of the challenges of contemporary life, such as environmental sustainability, social justice, health and wellbeing, and the use of new and old technologies in art and life, as a way of generating wider evidence of the societal value of dance, movement and embodied practice.   

The project is led by Professor Vida L Midgelow, Dean of UAL’s Doctoral School, and Dr Efrosini Protopapa, Director of Research at The Place.

PhD candidates will be registered with one of UAL’s colleges and will be supported by a joint team of supervisors from UAL and LCDS. Supervisors from UAL and The Place have strong expertise in practice research, PhD by published works (including practice), and collaborative doctoral awards with industry partners. See below potential areas of supervision.

Application Timeline

  • Applications for PhD projects starting in Sept 2027 will open in Autumn 2026
  • Application deadline to enrol in Sept 2027: 30 April 2027

The full assessment of your suitability and the availability of supervision can take some time, typically 2-3 months from submission of your application.

How to Apply

Step 1: Click the apply now button to visit the UAL application page

Step 2: When starting your application, please select your preferred UAL college and state ‘LCDS/UAL’ programme when asked for the title of the project in the form

Other application routes:

  • Transfer MPhil and PhD from another institution: If you're currently registered on a degree programme at another university and would like to discuss transferring to UAL/The Place, please get in touch with UAL's research team at researchdegrees@arts.ac.uk.
  • Research degree by published work: We can consider applications for a programme of research degree by published work at any point in the year, where applicants demonstrate research outputs that make a substantial contribution to knowledge. For further information and details please contact the UAL research team at researchdegrees@arts.ac.uk

Additional Information

Your research proposal is the most critical component of your research degree application. It will form the basis for discussion at your interview, and if your application is successful your proposal will also be used as the starting point for the Registration process.

Use the personal statement section of the online application form to tell us anything you couldn't express in the rest of the application within a 500 word limit.

Watch our webinar on how to put together a research proposal.

Areas of Supervision

We offer supervision expertise in areas that include, but are not limited to, the following:

Creative practice and producing in context
  • Conditions of production and postproduction, value and consumption, political economy and neoliberalism 
  • Improvisation and collaborative strategies and theories, authorship and collectivity 
  • Participation and communities, co-creation and accessibility  
  • Leadership in the arts, organisational structure and institutional critique  
  • Enchantment, perception, ritual, gesture, protest and carnival 
  • Outdoor practice and training, environmental arts practice and activism 
Dance through a cross-arts and interdisciplinary lens 
  • The body in sculpture, fashion and design, film and video, literature, music and visual arts  
  • Dramaturgy, curation, dance in galleries and museums 
  • Sound and music in performance, sonic arts, contemporary music and movement 
  • Screendance, moving image, cinematography and documentary film-making 
  • Science and art collaborations, movement in digital arts practices and computing 
  • Radical pedagogies, experimental and critical approaches to education and training 
Contemporary practice in relation to histories and archives 
  • Articulation of practice, scores, manifestos, performative and reflective writing  
  • Critical Approaches to the archive, embodied legacies, appropriation and repertoire  
  • Conceptual art, Fluxus, Judson Dance Theatre and histories of the avant-garde  
  • Video art, experimental film and television histories
  • Decolonising, repairing and activating the archive
Methodologies, contexts and theoretical approaches
  • Practice research and performative methodologies 
  • Cultural Studies, Critical Theory, Performance Theory and Psychoanalytic theory
  • Dance and Politics, Decolonialism, Racial Capitalism, Feminist, Marxist, Queer Approaches to Performance 
  • Dance anthropology, auto-ethnography, sensory ethnography, Story and Storytelling 
  • Posthumanism, ecology, ("new") materialisms and performing arts

Camden Partner Schools Programme

Trailer

With over 19 years’ experience as a classroom teacher, this is one of the most, if not THE most, inspiring, aspirational and engaging experiences for all children.

Assistant Head Teacher, West Hampstead Primary School

Over the past ten years, The Place has engaged with 21 local primary schools in Camden, engaging approximately 4,300 children in a dynamic programme of creative dance activities. Our aim is to immerse children in the joy of dance and empower teachers with the skills and confidence to incorporate dance into their school’s curriculum for the long term.

The Partner School package for 2026-2027 costs £1,300. The programme is designed for two participating classes in your school and includes:

  • Welcome Workshop: A visit to The Place where children get to take part in an introductory dance workshop and observe the fulltime students in their dance classes
  • Professional Dance Performance: Tickets for both classes to attend a professional dance show in our theatre
  • Creative Project: 20 hours of in-school creative dance sessions led by our team of skilled and experienced dance artists. This project is cross-curricular – designed to enhance and expand learning that is already taking place in the classroom – and culminates in the creation of a short dance piece that our artists help the children to make
  • Camden Partner Schools Festival: Children return to The Place to perform their dance creations in our theatre with costumes, lighting, and an audience of almost 300! The performance is professionally filmed and shared with each school
  • In-School Performance: An up-close performance in your school hall by students from London Contemporary Dance School, with a facilitated Q&A
  • CPD: 1.5-3 hours of bespoke teacher CPD, designed to suit the needs of either the whole staff group or specific class teachers
  • Learning resources: Access to online resources that encourage learning through the use of creative movement

records.title: Anatomy of Survival
records.description:
A woman walks into a cafe. She orders a coffee. The barista doesn't understand her request. The woman loses her sh*t. Chaos reigns. 

This offbeat collaboration between award-winning playwright Vivienne Franzmann and choreographer and psychotherapist Frauke Requardt, brings together 22 very different eyewitness accounts of one everyday altercation to show how our nervous systems are stuck in the Stone Age. 

Performed by two dancers, an actor and a drummer (and one bear). Anatomy of Survival is a show for all the nervous systems in the auditorium. Come and feel the rise and fall of yours.

Jeeves Takes Charge

Book Now
First seen 45 years ago, the Olivier Award-winning and much-loved Jeeves Takes Charge returns to London for a short season at the Charing Cross Theatre after showcase productions at the Jermyn Street Theatre (“Brilliant” – Jeffrey Archer), The Tabard Theatre (“How on earth does he do that?” – Trevor Nunn), and a Christmas season at the Theatre Royal, Bath (“One of this year’s Top 20 Christmas shows – The Guardian.) West End, Chichester and RSC favourite, Sam Harrison, plays all twenty-two much-loved PG Wodehouse characters including Jeeves, Wooster, Florence Craye, Gussie Fink-Nottle, Bingo Little, Uncle Willoughby, Aunt Dahlia, and many more – in a bravura, tour de force, one-man performance. 

Originally brought into the West End by Barbara Dickson and Bernard Theobald, together with Cameron Mackintosh and Andrew Lloyd Webber, Jeeves Takes Charge is guaranteed to put a smile on your face and a song in your heart.

Do not miss this dazzling and extraordinary, strictly limited, run. Pip Pip!

by PG Wodehouse

Lighting by Tim Mitchell

Design by Caite Hevner
Directed by Hugh Wooldridge
Produced by Steven M. Levy for Charing Cross Theatre Productions LTD.

In short, I can tell you that with absolute certainty you will be in for a ‘top hole, smashing, wizard, evening’, which after two hours will leave you breathless and dizzy with joy at the performance you have just been privileged to witness.

Theatre and Tonic ★★★★★

A welcome return then for Wodehouse aficionados and perhaps a useful introduction for newcomers, this lavish production features a remarkable central performance.

West End Best Friend

Harrison is excellent. He is clearly at home with both Wodehouse’s writing and this particular style of comedy. His bumbling delivery, physical comedy, rubbery movements and wonderfully eccentric mannerisms make him perfectly suited to the material.

Staged Theatre

Wooldridge’s staging is quite masterful, right up to curtain call during which Harrison takes his bow surrounded by the portraits of all the characters he has played.

The Spy in the Stalls

Harrison is magnetic, effortlessly funny and boldly dynamic.

All That Dazzles

once the production begins, the room changes to various locations and venues thanks to a wonderful combination of video projection, sound and lighting (compliments of Caite Hevner, Paul Groothuis and Tim Mitchell) in a way that is both shocking and outstanding. Truly superb work by the creatives.

London Theatre 1 ★★★★

With clever staging and a mesmerising performance, Jeeves Takes Charge is full of laughs from beginning to end.

North West End UK ★★★★

It’s nothing less than a tour de force and a model of infectious light entertainment.

Fairy Powered Productions ★★★★

A highly enjoyable night at the theatre.

A Youngish Perspective ★★★★

The staging is immaculately put together. Caite Hevner’s design is clever and dynamic.

First Night Magazine

It was truly an enjoyable evening, and the funniest performance I’ve seen for some time.

Theatre South East

for fans of the Wodehouse brand of comedy, this is an astute and appealing adaptation.

Theatre Weekly ★★★★

Funny, inventive and incredibly skilful, this is storytelling and multi-role performance at its very best.

Theatre Audience Podcast ★★★★

The combined effect is bright, lively and ephemeral, effectively catching the spirit of Jeeves and Wooster’s breezily carefree world.

The Stage

a delightfully lighthearted and entertaining show. Something we need more of right now.

Broadway World

a fun, very reverent take on the works of P.G Wodehouse, with a great physical performance from Sam Harrison.

The Theatre Flyer

the biggest achievement of the evening comes from Sam Harrison. The sheer amount of content he has to handle is extraordinary. He plays 22 (!) roles, switching between them and rattling through a near-impossible number of lines with great stamina. Harrison's technical skill is so admirable

Jack Stage

About Us

Opened in 2008, Lightbox is a 3 roomed club venue located in Lambeth, South London. The 600 capacity space takes its name from the LED walls that cover the club’s main room. Lightbox regularly plays host to techno, house, UK garage and drum & bass. The club regularly runs Thursday night events and after-hours parties in addition to regular weekend club nights. With a recently installed, brand new soundsystem supplied by Danley Sound Labs expect state of the art sound & lighting.

Lightbox events

Saturday 6th November 2021 - 11:00pm til 6:00am

Enquiries

Lightbox London, 6 South Lambeth Place, London SW8 1SP

Please choose your enquiry type below and submit the relevant details in the form.

If you want to contact us please use the form below.

If you want to book an area at one of our events, please contact us using the form below.

Contact us about lost property using the form below.

FAQs  

We do not allow any unauthorised filming or photograph. You will not be allowed to bring in professional cameras. If you would like permission to film or take photos please email info@lightboxlondon.com

Lightbox London is always looking for staff to join our team. If you are looking for work please send your CV to info@lightboxlondon.com

Yes you can. However, all medication and equipment will need to be registered with our on-site medics provided it is in the manufacturer's original packaging. We strongly encourage that all medication and medical equipment is stored with our on-site medics wherever possible, and that you use our medic room when administering any medication. The medics will show you the area we use exclusively for our medics and any member of staff or security can escort you to the medic room should you need to use the area.

You can buy tickets for Lightbox London through our website – please click on the What's On tab.

It couldn’t be easier to find Lightbox London – we are in the transport hub at Vauxhall. We are less than 100 metres from Vauxhall Underground Station.

Underground – Victoria Line

Overground – various train services

You can use Transport for London’s website to plan your journey www.tfl.gov.uk

There is no local parking and Lightbox London recommends using public transport to get to us.

Lightbox London has a strict over 18 policy.

We also operate a No ID No Entry policy – this means no matter how old you are you must present valid ID to gain admission to the venue.

Valid ID must be in date. We accept the following forms of identification;

  • Valid Passport
  • Valid Driving Licence
  • Valid National ID card
  • Valid ID with PASS hologram (find our more information at pass-scheme.org.uk)

Please note that we do not accept photos of ID or photocopies.

Yes Lightbox London is an accessible venue, although there are some parts of the venue which are not accessible via wheelchair due to steps.

Please feel free to email us at info@lightboxlondon.com if you have an specific access needs.

Lightbox London has various events with various music policies. The best thing to do is check our What's on section.

The dress code at Lightbox London is casual. There are different rules for certain events however, so best to call or email us to find out more. 

We do not allow people to wear hoods in the queue or in the venue.

Lightbox London operates various events with various opening times. The best thing to do is check out the event listings in the What's on section.

If you think you have lost something at Lightbox London you can click on Contact Us and complete the lost property form. Please make your description as detailed as possible to help us.

Please note we hold property for 3 months and then it is donated to charity.

All ID documents and mobile phones are handed to the local Police.

Venue Hire

Vauxhall Arches is a collection of 10 railway arches close to the River Thames. Only 20 yards from Vauxhall Underground, Rail and 24-hour Bus Station, the venue is well known and easily accessible.

Close to the banks of the River Thames under Vauxhalls railway arches possibility can flow freely and spontaneity has more than enough room to dance.

A versatile space with multiple rooms, outdoor areas and VIP spaces, catering for events of varying capacity, our team are happy to accommodate your individual requirements.

Vauxhall Arches are available for external hire throughout the year. Now regarded as one of London's leading clubbing destinations, we offer a multi-functional and flexible interlocking space for your event or production.

Get in touch

Lightbox London, 6 South Lambeth Place, London SW8 1SP

Check out our sister club: firelondon.net | Privacy Policy

Upcoming events

Artisan Market – Saturday 5th September 10am -2pm

 

Discover Epsom & Ewell u3a - Poster Exhibition 5 - 12 September

Visit the u3a exhibition in the Bourne Hall foyer from 5–12 September and explore a taster of the many interest groups on offer. Learn about our history, discover our current activities, and find out about our future plans.

Why not stop by and see what Epsom & Ewell u3a has to offer?

Museum Kids Club - Victorian Shopping - Saturday 12th September 1- 2.30pm

Step into the world of shopping and trading at this fun, hands-on Kids’ Club session. Become a shopkeeper or a customer and decide what you would sell, buy and even eat!

A fun and educational activity for curious young minds, packed with imaginative play and learning.

What will your shop sell? Come along and find out!

Recommended for children ages 8 - 12+

Children must be supervised for the duration of the event

For more information, contact Susan Dalloe, sdalloe@epsom-ewell.gov.uk 020 8394 1734

Book your tickets here: https://sessami.co/events/victorian-shopping

 

Transport Bizarre - Saturday 12th September, 10:30-14:30

 

Collectables Transport Fair at Bourne Hall on Saturday 12th September

Transport enthusiasts and collectors are invited to the Collectables Transport Fair at Bourne Hall, Spring Street, Ewell, Surrey (KT17 1UF) on Saturday 12th September 2026. Open from 10:30am to 2:30pm, this fair brings together a wide range of stalls selling railway and bus memorabilia, including model railways, diecast vehicles, collectables, and a variety of other transport-related items.

Admission is £3, with free entry for under-16s, making it a great day out for families and hobbyists alike. A large pay-and-display car park is located adjacent to the venue, and Bourne Hall is easily accessible by public transport, with local bus routes stopping nearby and Ewell West station just a five-minute walk away.Whether you are a serious collector or simply enjoy transport history, the Collectables Transport Fair offers plenty to browse, buy, and enjoy in a welcoming community setting.

For more information contact ttbazaars@btinternet.com or 07753146674 or 07508152754.

 

Be in Includer Exhibition - Celebrating National Inclusion Week in collaboration with Include Choir - 14 - 19 September

 

Celebrate National Inclusion Week with 'Be an Includer' an exhibition at Bourne Hall created in collaboration with Include Choir. Discover how we can help create welcoming communities for people with understanding and/or speaking difficulties, and learn simple ways to ensure everyone feels valued and included.

Include Choir Performance - Saturday 19th September 2.30 - 3pm

To mark the end of Inclusion Week and the exhibition, Include Choir will present a special performance on Saturday, bringing their unique blend of music, inclusive communication and joy.

Come along and experience the feeling of being included.

 

Heritage Open Days at Bourne Hall Museum

Book your tickets by following this link: https://sessami.co/EmoDSpuIfJgflQ7uaNajXRyHq9A3

Sunday 13 September 11am

Epsom salts and spa walk

Join Ian West on a guided walk exploring how the discovery of Epsom Salts transformed Epsom into a thriving spa town, uncovering its history, notable residents and surviving landmarks.

 

Monday 14 September 2pm

Everyday histories in Worcester Park from the Iron Age to the Computer Age talk

Join David Rymill for an illustrated journey through Worcester Park’s history, from early settlements and Nonsuch Palace to the railway, suburbia and pioneering local industries.

 

Tuesday 15 September 10am

Life on the Downs walk

Join former professional jockey Caroline Baldock for a guided walk of The Derby course, sharing its history, scandals and the evolution of the thoroughbred horse.

 

Wednesday 16 September 2pm

Lost buildings of Epsom talk

Join Ian West for an illustrated talk exploring how Epsom grew from a small settlement into a fashionable spa town, highlighting its historic buildings and changing townscape.

 

Thursday 17 September 10am

People and places walk

Join Ruth Munns for a fascinating walk through Ewell Village, uncovering its famous residents, local history and surprising stories from the past.

 

Thursday 17 September 2pm

Token Coins in Ewell and Epsom: A History Talk

Join Ian Franklin as he explores how people in Ewell and Epsom coped with coin shortages by creating and using their own currency - featuring local specimens, tokens and counterfeit coins.

 

Country and Western Social Events - Friday 25th September - 19.30 - 22.30

Pull on your cowboy boots and join Hillbilly Gill & Frankie Lou for a lively night of line dancing, great music, plenty of laughs, and drinks from the bar to keep the party going!

Whether you’re a complete beginner or a seasoned dancer, our friendly instructors will have you stepping, stomping, and swinging across the dance floor in no time. So grab a drink, round up your friends, and get ready for a fantastic evening of country fun!

There are 3 dates booked for the year. Book your tickets for the September event here: https://sessami.co/events/country-western-social-september?utm_medium=website&utm_source=Bourne%20Hall%20

 

Museum Kids Club - Epsom Salts, Spa and Wallpaper - Saturday 10th October 1- 2.30pm

How did a cow discover Epsom Salts? What happened when Epsom was a Spa town? Find out more and design your very own wallpaper.

Recommended for children ages 8 - 12+

Children must be supervised for the duration of the event

For more information, contact Susan Dalloe, sdalloe@epsom-ewell.gov.uk 020 8394 1734

Book your tickets here: Bourne Hall | Bourne Hall, Spring Street, Ewell, Epsom, UK | Sessami

 

Country and Western Social Events - Friday 23rd October - 19.30 - 22.30

Pull on your cowboy boots and join Hillbilly Gill & Frankie Lou for a lively night of line dancing, great music, plenty of laughs, and drinks from the bar to keep the party going!

Whether you’re a complete beginner or a seasoned dancer, our friendly instructors will have you stepping, stomping, and swinging across the dance floor in no time. So grab a drink, round up your friends, and get ready for a fantastic evening of country fun!

Book your tickets here: Country and Western Social Nights October | Sessami

 

Museum Kids Club - WW1 Revisited - Saturday 14th November 1- 2.30pm

Join us to listen to the Captain’s tales of the war, handle real equipment and uniform!

Recommended for children ages 8 - 12+

Children must be supervised for the duration of the event

For more information, contact Susan Dalloe, sdalloe@epsom-ewell.gov.uk 020 8394 1734

Book your tickets here: Bourne Hall | Bourne Hall, Spring Street, Ewell, Epsom, UK | Sessami  

 

Christmas Light Switch on at Bourne Hall - Saturday 28 November - 3 - 6.30pm

More information to follow!

 

Museum Kids Club -Traditional Decorations - Saturday 12th December 1- 2.30pm

How did people enjoy the winter season in Victorian and Edwardian times ? Come along and make your own decorations to take home with you.

Recommended for children ages 8 - 12+

Children must be supervised for the duration of the event

For more information, contact Susan Dalloe, sdalloe@epsom-ewell.gov.uk 020 8394 1734
