PERFORMANCES

Globe Theatre

Experience our world-renowned, open-air theatre

A Midsummer Night's Dream

29 August
Join us under starry summer skies for ‘the ultimate communal celebration’ ★★★★★ (Sunday Mirror) and be part of the magic of Shakespeare’s comedy.
Info & Tickets
Globe Theatre

Much Ado About Nothing

31 August - 24 October
In sun-soaked Messina, sharp tongues, short tempers and savage gossip collide in an unfiltered rom-com about secrets, status and second chances.
Info & Tickets
Globe Theatre

Love's Labour's Lost

29 August - 13 September
A new production by Indiana Lown-Collins, bringing the passion of flamenco to this refreshingly human comedy about desire, love, and connection.
Info & Tickets
Globe Theatre

As You Like It

9 September - 25 October
Co‑directed by Sean Holmes (Pinocchio, Globe) and Charlie Josephine (Cowbois, RSC/Royal Court), this bold new As You Like It bursts with lust, love, and live music.
Info & Tickets
Globe Theatre

Pinocchio

28 November - 3 January
Following its smash-hit premiere in 2025, our ★★★★★ ‘beautiful new musical brimming with fun and magic’ (WhatsOnStage) returns in winter 2026.
Info & Tickets
Globe Theatre

Sam Wanamaker Playhouse

Step inside London’s only candlelit theatre

A World Elsewhere

29 - 30 August
Don’t miss our ‘imaginative, heartfelt and utterly captivating’ ★★★★★ (Broadway World) new family show before the summer holidays end.
Info & Tickets
Sam Wanamaker Playhouse

Julius Caesar

6 November - 14 February
Take your place as a citizen of Rome, and experience Shakespeare’s epic thriller Julius Caesar in the intimate, candlelit setting of the Sam Wanamaker Playhouse. 
Info & Tickets
Sam Wanamaker Playhouse

The Animals Come to the Table

11 December - 24 January
The world premiere of a bold new play from one of the UK’s leading playwrights, Timberlake Wertenbaker, written for the candlelit Sam Wanamaker Playhouse.
Info & Tickets
Sam Wanamaker Playhouse

The Seagull

15 January - 10 April
Caroline Steinbeis and Rory Mullarkey (Three Sisters) reunite for Anton Chekhov’s timeless story of ambition, ego and desire in the candlelit Sam Wanamaker Playhouse.
Info & Tickets
Sam Wanamaker Playhouse

King John

20 February - 11 April
Experience Shakespeare’s rarely performed masterpiece King John in the intimate, candlelit Sam Wanamaker Playhouse, directed by Jaz Woodcock-Stewart.   
Info & Tickets
Sam Wanamaker Playhouse

Globe Young Company 2026: Pineapple

10 - 11 October
Discover a brand-new play by Anne Odeke (Princess Essex, Globe) performed by the Globe Young Company for Shakespeare and Race Festival 2026.
Shakespeare and Race
Info & Tickets

TALKS

Essential conversations exploring the work we do in relation to the world we live in

The Globe Talks: Love's Labour's Lost

2 September
Delve into Shakespeare's refreshingly human comedy with members of our upcoming production's creative team. Includes Q&A.
The Globe Talks
Info & Tickets
Bankside

The Globe Talks: As You Like It

16 September
In this panel discussion and Q&A, join members of the show’s creative team, as we delve into the world of As You Like It and explore its key themes.
The Globe Talks
Info & Tickets
Bankside

Pineapple: Post-Show Talk

11 October
Delve deeper into new play Pineapple with this post-show talk exploring the play’s themes, characters, and rehearsal process. Includes Q&A.
Shakespeare and Race
Info & Tickets

The Globe Talks: Pinocchio

29 December
In a panel discussion and Q&A, listen to members of the show’s creative team, as we delve into the world of our festive musical Pinocchio and explore its key themes.
The Globe Talks
Info & Tickets
Bankside

The Globe Talks: The Animals Come to the Table

22 January
In a panel discussion and Q&A, listen to members of the show’s creative team, as we explore the world premiere of Timberlake Wertenbaker's The Animals Come to the Table and its key themes.
The Globe Talks
Info & Tickets
Bankside

The Globe Talks: Julius Caesar

29 January
In a panel discussion and Q&A, listen to members of the show’s creative team, as we delve into the world of Julius Caesar and explore its key themes.
The Globe Talks
Info & Tickets
Bankside

The Globe Talks: The Seagull

11 March
In a panel discussion and Q&A, listen to members of the show’s creative team, as we explore this production of Chekhov's The Seagull and its key themes.
The Globe Talks
Info & Tickets
Bankside

The Globe Talks: King John

7 April
In a panel discussion and Q&A, listen to members of the show’s creative team, as we delve into the world of Shakespeare's rarely performed masterpiece King John and explore its key themes.
The Globe Talks
Info & Tickets
Bankside

GUIDED TOURS

Discover Shakespeare’s iconic, open-air theatre or uncover the history of Bankside with our Guided Tours

Globe Theatre Guided Tour

29 August - 31 January
This unique experience brings to life 400 years of history and transports you back to Shakespeare’s London with a guided tour of the Globe Theatre.
Guided Tours
Info & Tickets
Globe Theatre

Premium Globe Guided Tour

7 November - 31 January
An unparalleled experience that transports you back to Shakespeare’s London with an exclusive view from the Globe Theatre stage.
Guided Tours
Info & Tickets

Pride Guided Tour

31 August - 25 January
Step inside our iconic wooden ‘O’ for a special tour that brings to life the queer characters and stories from Shakespeare's life and writing, and Elizabethan London.
Guided Tours
Info & Tickets
Bankside

Shakespeare's Walking Tour

29 August - 31 October
This unique experience includes a walking tour of Bankside, London’s original theatre district bringing 400 years of thrilling history to life.
Guided Tours
Info & Tickets

Ghosts & Ghouls Family Tour

5 September - 30 January
This special family-friendly, spooky guided tour of the Globe Theatre brings to life the ghosts, spirits and scary happenings of Shakespeare’s most chilling plays.
Info & Tickets

Twilight Walking Tour

6 November - 29 January
Explore the Bankside area and be transported back to London's 'Kingdom of Night' and discover Shakespeare's fascination with the dark.
Guided Tours
Info & Tickets
Bankside

Shakespeare's True Crimes Walking Tour

4 September - 30 January
Explore the streets around the Globe with expert Guides and discover the intriguing criminal history of the Bankside area and its people, including Shakespeare himself. 
Info & Tickets
Bankside

Heaven to Hell Tour

29 August - 10 April
Become a Member (from £5 a month) to unlock our backstage tours. Guided by an experienced production team member, view the thatched roof up close, walk the stage, and venture into the Globe's hidden depths.
Info & Tickets
Globe Theatre

Much Ado About Nothing: Guided Tour

1 September - 22 October
This unique Much Ado About Nothing themed Guided Tour of the Globe Theatre delves into the history, characters and themes of Shakespeare’s comedy of wit and wooing.
Guided Tours
Info & Tickets

Group Guided Tour

ONGOING GLOBE THEATRE

Your group can enjoy our Globe Theatre Guided Tour with a discounted ticket rate.

DISCOVER MORE

CLIMATE ACTION

Visit our Sustainability page for more details

The Animals Come to the Table

11 December - 24 January
The world premiere of a bold new play from one of the UK’s leading playwrights, Timberlake Wertenbaker, written for the candlelit Sam Wanamaker Playhouse.
Info & Tickets
Sam Wanamaker Playhouse

MakeBeth

24 October - 1 November
A brand-new interactive retelling of Shakespeare’s Macbeth brought to life with recycled cardboard magic. Perfect for families and young audiences aged 7+.
Info & Tickets
Bankside

FAMILY EVENTS & TOURS

Bring the whole family to experience the wonders of Shakespeare

View All Family Events

MakeBeth

24 October - 1 November
A brand-new interactive retelling of Shakespeare’s Macbeth brought to life with recycled cardboard magic. Perfect for families and young audiences aged 7+.
Info & Tickets
Bankside

Macbeth: On Stage Family Workshop (9-11 years)

26 - 31 October
Bring Macbeth to life in this fun and practical workshop on one of our unique stages. This workshop is for young people aged 9-11 and their grown-ups.
Info & Tickets

Twelfth Night: Family Workshop (5-8 years)

27 - 31 October
Bring Shakespeare's whirlwind comedy to life in this fun and practical workshop aimed at children aged 5–8 and their grown-ups.
Info & Tickets
Bankside

Ghosts & Ghouls Family Tour

5 September - 30 January
This special family-friendly, spooky guided tour of the Globe Theatre brings to life the ghosts, spirits and scary happenings of Shakespeare’s most chilling plays.
Info & Tickets

Twelfth Night: Family Workshop (9-11 Years)

27 - 31 October
Bring Shakespeare's whirlwind comedy to life in this fun and practical workshop aimed at children aged 9–11 and their grown-ups.
Info & Tickets
Bankside

A World Elsewhere: Family Workshop (9-11 years)

29 - 30 August
Explore the power of imagination, friendship, and fearless creativity through interactive games and storytelling activities inspired by the show. For ages 9-11 and their grown ups.
Info & Tickets
Bankside

A World Elsewhere: Family Workshop (5-8 years)

29 - 30 August
Explore the power of imagination, friendship, and fearless creativity through interactive games and storytelling activities inspired by the show.
Info & Tickets
Bankside

Sword Fighting Demonstration

29 August - 29 October
The Globe's expert Fight Team bring Early Modern stage combat to life, with the chance to handle the weapons yourself!
Info & Tickets

RESEARCH EVENTS

Delve deeper into Shakespeare’s world and works with our research events

Research in Action: Editing in Action

17 September
Join us in the Sam Wanamaker Playhouse for a lively exploration of how performance can illuminate and reshape the way we edit Shakespeare.
Info & Tickets
Sam Wanamaker Playhouse

Research in Action: Global Early Modern Stage

7 October
Join this special workshop in the Sam Wanamaker Playhouse which invites us to reconsider the global nature of early modern English drama.
Info & Tickets
Sam Wanamaker Playhouse

Symposium: Contested Futures

16 - 17 October
A two-day symposium bringing together international scholars to explore the contested meanings of Shakespeare in our present and future.
Info & Tickets

Youths That Thunder

29 October
Dr Eli Cumings (King's College London) and Dr Lydia Valentine (Shakespeare's Globe) present new research for anyone curious about Shakespeare, race, and performance. 
Shakespeare and Race
Info & Tickets
Sam Wanamaker Playhouse

Samurai Othello: Sharing and Discussion

20 October
Shakespeare meets Samurai as New Earth Theatre and Shakespeare's Globe present a work-in-progress sharing and panel discussion of Othello, set in medieval Japan.
Shakespeare and Race
Info & Tickets

Shakespeare and Windrush

22 October
A roundtable discussion bringing together creatives, historians and literary scholars to celebrate the contributions of the British Caribbean community to literature, theatre and performance. 
Shakespeare and Race
Info & Tickets

YOUNG PEOPLE

Events for young aspiring actors and academics

View All Young People Events

Young Actors Short Course (11-13 years)

26 October - 6 April
A lively and practical course designed to bring Shakespeare to life in new, exciting ways. For young performers aged 11–13.
Info & Tickets
Bankside

Young Actors Short Course (8–10 years)

26 October - 6 April
A lively and practical course designed to bring Shakespeare to life in new, exciting ways. For young performers aged 8–10.
Young People
Info & Tickets
Bankside

Othello: A Level Boost

17 October
An interactive A Level workshop exploring Othello through an anti-racist lens, developing key skills for essays and exams through performance-based activities.
Info & Tickets

Romeo and Juliet: GCSE Revision Boost

7 November - 6 February
Supercharge your GCSE revision of Romeo and Juliet in this practical session, designed for ages 14–16.
Young People
Info & Tickets

Macbeth: GCSE Revision Boost

12 September - 6 March
Supercharge your GCSE revision of Shakespeare’s bloody tragedy Macbeth in this practical GCSE Boost day designed for ages 14–16, who have already studied the play.
Info & Tickets
Bankside

Macbeth: Workshop (12-16 years)

26 - 30 October
Bring Macbeth to life in this practical and interactive workshop designed for 12-16 year olds. Ideal for young people with an interest in drama or literature.
Info & Tickets
Bankside

Hamlet: Workshop (14-16 years)

24 - 31 October
Deep-dive into Shakespeare’s famous tragedy Hamlet in this practical workshop designed for ages 14–16.
Info & Tickets
Bankside

Othello: On Stage Workshop (17-19 years)

26 - 31 October
Bring Shakespeare's tragedy to life yourself on the unique Sam Wanamaker Playhouse stage. For ages 17–19.
Info & Tickets
Globe Theatre

Romeo and Juliet: On Stage Workshop (14-16 years)

28 - 30 October
Bring Shakespeare's Romeo and Juliet to life in this practical workshop on one of our unique stages. For young people aged 14-16 with an interest in theatre or performing.
Young People
Info & Tickets
Sam Wanamaker Playhouse

TEACHER TRAINING

Opportunities to continue professional development

View All Teacher Training

Teaching Shakespeare Through Performance

19 - 30 July
Join our flagship teacher training course for continuing professional development. Over two weeks, take part in classroom workshops, seminars, lectures and rehearsals, and watch performances in the iconic Globe Theatre
Info & Tickets

Online CPD: Teaching Anti-Racist Shakespeare

6 October - 9 February
Learn new skills to build an anti-racist approach to teaching Shakespeare in the classroom in this practical online CPD workshop, designed for Secondary English and Drama teachers.
Info & Tickets
At Home

Online CPD: Teaching Shakespeare and Sexuality

2 February
Build your confidence in facilitating LGBTQIA+ inclusive discussions in the classroom in this interactive online workshop. For Secondary English and Drama teachers.
Info & Tickets
At Home

28 September
Join this CPD session for English teachers and learn new classroom tools and techniques to deepen students’ understanding of Romeo and Juliet.
Info & Tickets

Online CPD: Teaching Shakespeare and Women

9 March
An online CPD to develop your approach to classroom conversations about Shakespeare's depictions of women.
Info & Tickets
At Home

CPD: Teaching Macbeth at KS4: In Person or Online

19 January
Join this interactive session to enhance your classroom teaching of Shakespeare’s epic tragedy at Key Stage 4. This is a hybrid event – choose to attend in-person at Shakespeare’s Globe or online via Zoom.
Info & Tickets
At Home

Online CPD: Teaching Macbeth at Key Stage 4

14 October - 7 November
An online Continuing Professional Development session hosted on Zoom to enhance your classroom teaching of Macbeth at Key Stage 4.
Info & Tickets

Online CPD: Teaching Romeo and Juliet at KS4

28 September
Join this CPD session for English teachers and learn new classroom tools and techniques to deepen students’ understanding of Romeo and Juliet.

VENUE HIRE

Host your event at one of the most unique venues in London.

 

  • Our Spaces
  • Bespoke Events
  • Swan at the Globe

s

 

hakespeare’s Globe welcomes events, from small, intimate gatherings to large-scale corporate hires for up to 450 guests. We accommodate networking, conferences, exhibitions, presentations, product launches, celebrations and more. With an enviable location on London’s Southbank, the Globe is one of the most recognisable and memorable spaces for private hire in London. Plus, by choosing to host your event with us, you are helping to support our amazing work on and off our stages.

Shakespeare’s Globe is not only situated in an ideal location, but the venue brings together a range of stunning spaces, creative gastronomy, and exclusive access to world-class theatre; all combining to create a one-off, immersive event experience for you and your guests.

To find out more, please get in touch using the enquiry button below.

OUR SPACES

The Globe Theatre

Throughout the summer season, the Globe is home to multiple productions and performances with audiences up to 1500. The most recognisable and largest of our spaces, the theatre may be hired for filming, photography as well as private hires and celebrations.

Sam Wanamaker Playhouse

One of the only candlelit theatres in Europe, the Sam Wanamaker Playhouse is the perfect setting to host an unforgettable event. The space can host 200 guests for lectures, presentations, and corporate events.

The Education Studios

The Education Studios are located on 1-2 Bear Gardens, SE1 9ED, perfectly situated just around the corner from our theatres. The studios have a range of spaces suitable for smaller events of up to 35 people and can accommodate meetings, workshops and away days. The Perry Studio is the largest of the spaces and can hold 80 people.

Upper Foyer

This semi-private space is perfect for a relaxed drinks reception of up to 60 people. The space can be yours to use exclusively for events or for group visits to performances.

Main Foyer pictured

Lecture Theatre and Lower Foyer

Our newly renovated Lecture Theatre can seat up to 120 people and is perfect for smaller, private presentations and lectures.

The Lower Foyer, situated just outside, is available to hire alongside for receptions, as a breakout space or for welcoming guests. Both rooms have step free access.

BESPOKE EVENTS

Tours

Give your attendees a private tour of Shakespeare’s Globe and discover the stories and secrets of our open-air theatre, how the Globe battled to survive plague, fire and political oppression, and how one man’s vision saw it rise again after 400 years.

Historical Demonstrations

Enjoy dynamic demonstrations from our specialists, including costume design and sword fighting. Whether as part of a schedule of activities or a one-off experience, our in-house experts can organise demonstrations specially tailored for your group.

Presentations and Panel Events

Whether you’d like to treat your guests with a talk or share expert insights from the Globe’s world-renowned experts, this is a fantastic way to create a truly memorable event bringing the magic of the Globe directly to your group.

Private Box Hire

Our exclusive boxes are the perfect way to entertain an intimate group of guests for a memorable night at the theatre, including delicious seasonal private dining in Swan London.

Performance

If you are looking to really impress your guests and make an unforgettable event, treat your attendees to a performance of one of our critically-acclaimed productions.

Workshops and Team Building

Whether you want an ice-breaker at the start of an away day or something to get everyone up on their feet after a long meeting, these tailored workshops provide an interactive and thought-provoking link between the world of Shakespeare and your team. Find out more about our Executive Training Programme, Centre Stage.

Spaces at The Swan

The team Swan at the Globe have a wealth of experience in delivering stylish evening events and functions for any occasion. They have several private dining spaces available for hire, including the beautiful Balcony Room overlooking the Thames, and the Underglobe.

Globe Theatre

The ‘hilarious and heartfelt’ ★★★★ (The Guardian) A Midsummer Night’s Dream is now playing in London’s Globe Theatre, and you’re invited to be part of the magic.

Director Emily Lim’s ‘joyful staging’ ★★★★ (The Times) of Shakespeare’s comedy is ‘the ultimate communal celebration’ ★★★★★ (Sunday Mirror).

As night deepens on the eve of a royal wedding, a company of amateur performers prepares a play for the big day and invite you to step into their story.

Follow the players, lovers and fairies into the forest where hearts open, spells go awry and surprising transformations unfold. By dawn, everyone has been changed.

Book your tickets for ‘irresistible fun’ ★★★★ (Financial Times) and ‘good vibes only’ ★★★★ (Time Out) under starry, summer skies.

‘Are we all met?’

GO OFF-GRID ON 28 JUNE

For this special performance during London Climate Action Week, the Globe Theatre will go off-grid on Sunday 28 June at 1.00pm.

We’re switching off and returning to our Shakespearean roots, exploring how far we can move toward a low-energy production, and how we might bring this approach to more of our performances in future.

Guided by the daylight, as we would have been 400 years ago, this will be a live experiment in storytelling and sustainability. We’ll track our energy use, test new ways of working, and invite audiences to reconsider their own carbon footprint.

Planning a school visit?

2026 is the perfect year to bring your class to Shakespeare’s Globe.

Combine a performance with a practical and inspiring workshop tailored to the production, either in your school before or after your visit or in one of our rehearsal rooms on the day of the show.

School tickets are limited and must be requested via our online booking form. We’re expecting high demand so get your request in early for the best chance to secure tickets.

Welcome to the Newham Neighbours Programme at Stratford East. 

We believe theatre is for everyone, no matter your background, experiences, or financial circumstances. Even if you’ve never set foot in the theatre or you think it's not for you, we want to make sure you can come and check us out 

We want everyone in Newham to feel welcome at Stratford East. 

The best part? Everything we do is FREE! 

Newham Neighbours is open to all Newham residents aged 26+ (If you're under 26, check out our Young People’s Programme for opportunities available to you.) 

If you run a Community Organisation or Charity in Newham, you can also sign up as a Lead Contact to hear about opportunities. Click here to see more about what we can offer Newham Organisations. 

So, what are you waiting for? Join us, get involved, try out something new.  

Click here to sign up.

Completing this form means you will be added to the Newham Neighbours mailing list. This is managed by the Learning & Participation team at Stratford East, and is specific to projects, workshops, and events we run. We will email you with opportunities and information about how to get involved. You can unsubscribe anytime. 

 

What's on offer: 

COMMUNITY SOCIALS 
We love throwing open our doors to welcome our nearest neighbours! Our Community Socials are all about coming together with others from the area and gaining insight into the magic of theatre. They are a chance to meet new faces, reconnect with old friends, and have a great time together! 

FREE ADULT WORKSHOPS 
We have two workshops that we run regularly that are all about having fun, meeting others and perhaps learning some new skills. The workshops usually run for approximately 6 weeks.  

Adult Drama Workshops are fun, friendly and inclusive introduction classes, that are designed for people with no experience. There is no audition to take part, just a willingness to give it a go and try something new. Click here read more.

The Reading Room is for people who love a good chat and are interested in joining us here for a free breakfast, as we read extracts from plays, and talk about them! There is no need to be a confident reader and no experience is needed. Click here to read more. 

 
NEWHAM NEIGHBOURS TAKE YOUR SEATS  
We offer FREE tickets to Newham residents and local organisations for our productions! These tickets are perfect for first-time theatregoers or those who haven’t been to see a show with us yet. It’s our way of making theatre more accessible to our community. To hear about when there are tickets available, you will need to sign up to our mailing list. Priority is always given to first-time attendees, and all tickets are subject to availability. 

BESPOKE PROJECTS AND WORKSHOPS 
From time to time, we host special projects and workshops inspired by our stage productions. These opportunities are open to people on our mailing list, so make sure you’re signed up to stay in the loop. Don’t forget to follow @trse_getinvolved on Instagram for all the latest updates!

Schools Programme

 

SCHOOLS TECHNICAL THEATRE INSIGHT WORKSHOPS

Stratford East is pleased to offer Technical Theatre Insight Workshops to East London secondary schools. 

The 90-minute sessions are designed to develop GCSE and A-Level Drama students' understanding of lighting, sound and set design. The workshops will expand technical vocabulary and shed light on how backstage elements contribute to creating meaning and core themes in a mainstage production. 

This offer includes one 90 minute workshop plus free tickets to see a Stratford East production.   

*The maximum group size we can accommodate for a technical insight workshop is 30 students.* 

 


TEACHERS' NIGHT

We offer FREE tickets for Newham, Tower Hamlets, and Hackney teachers to Teachers' Nights at Stratford East. If you would be interested in joining us, please get in touch on getinvolved@stratfordeast.com

  

TICKET PRICES FOR SCHOOLS
Call our Box Office on 020 8534 0310 to secure the best deal, or email getinvolved@stratfordeast.com for more information.

WORKSHOPS
We are committed to supporting local Newham schools in enriching their curriculum and widening students’ experience and understanding of theatre. Please contact us if you have any questions. 

RESOURCES FOR YOU AND YOUR STUDENTS
We've created a series of resource packs designed to support the teaching of drama in secondary schools. You can download these free educational resources below.

Understanding The Creative Team
Designed to support students’ understanding of the creatives that are involved in making a production beyond those on stage. This resource looks at the Sound Designer, Lighting Designer, Stage Manager and Assistant Director. Download here or click the image below.

Performing Monologues 
Designed to help students to prepare, rehearse and perform a monologue. Download here or click the image below.

Designing Monologues 
These exercises will support students in exploring the early stages of the design process. Download here or click the image below.


TECHNICAL THEATRE RESOURCE PACK
Designed to develop teachers understanding of technical theatre, with practical exercises to use in the drama studio.
Download here

SHOW RESOURCE PACKS
Insights into the significance of and creation of shows to share with your students:
Cinderella
Red Riding Hood

ANTI-RACISM RESOURCE PACK FOR DRAMA EDUCATORS
Designed for drama teachers seeking to further their understanding of race, racism and anti-racist practice in the classroom. 
Download here 

ARTS MARK AND ARTS AWARD
Stratford East is an Arts Award supporter. We can provide support for young people with their Arts Award qualifications.

Our offer supports schools at any stage of their Artsmark journey to support and complement their drama provision.

BLOODSPORT: After Helen of Troy

THU 03 SEP - SAT 10 OCT 2026
Book
  • About
  • Booking Details
  • Cast & Creatives

GIVE IT BACK. GIVE IT BACK NOW. GIVE IT BACK OR I’LL TAKE IT BACK.

Artistic Director Lisa Spirling makes her directorial debut at Stratford East with this fierce new play by Ava Pickett (1536, Almeida Theatre, upcoming Baz Lurhmann film about Joan of Arc).  

Years after she walked out on her family, Helen has returned home after a war fought in her name. Her husband celebrates, her childhood friend Cee does not. Over the course of this first fragile night of peace time, wounds reopen, loyalties fracture and the true cost of a woman’s choice to leave her life is made clear.  

Ava Pickett’s debut play 1536 (Almeida Theatre) won the Susan Smith Blackburn Prize in 2024, received a special commendation from the George Devine Award, and won The Stage Debut Award (Best Writer). 1536 was also earned Ava nominations in The Standard Theatre Award’s Most Promising Playwright category in 2025, and the Critic Circle Theatre Award for Most Promising Playwright. Following a sold out run at the Almeida, 1536 will open on the West End in May 2026. It has also been picked up for a TV adaptation by the BBC.  

In addition, Ava has adapted Jane Austen’s Emma for the Rose Theatre, Kingston’s Autumn 2025 season, and her adaptation of A.K. Blakemore’s The Manningtree Witches opened at the Mercury Theatre Colchester in February 2026.  

Ava is co-writing a feature film based on the life of Joan of Arc, with Baz Luhrmann for Warner Brothers. Other screen credits include Brassic, The Buccaneers, The Great and How to Get to Heaven from Belfast. 

Presented by Stratford East.

 

This production is generously supported by Eleanor Lloyd Productions, Eilene Davidson Productions and Mark Gordon Pictures.
Supported by Cockayne Grants for the Arts, a Donor Advised Fund, held at The Prism Charitable Trust

WELCOME ABOARD!


WHAT'S ON

click on event to book

WELCOME ABOARD!


Our Mission


To create a world-class arts centre on a historic cargo ship in the old docks of Canary Wharf

Our Vision


Built in 1913 when London’s docks were filled with similar ships. It’s now one of the last ones left here. Restored and lovingly converted into a public arts centre the ship has a new lease of life. The cargo hold now holds a 100-seater theatre, a characterful bar, and an exhibition space.

It’s a unique space, in a really special part of London, and we really hope our programming reflects some of that. The docks have always introduced new things to London, and we’re keen to continue that history with events that highlight new and interesting voices, and bring new audiences to more established artists.

There's a special alchemy in ports - where people and ideas come from all over the world and mix - it's part of what makes East London so special and our project hopes to mirror that. We aim for an events programme where people and ideas can continue to mix. We want to provide a space for the interdisciplinary, the underepresented, and the experimental, and a shared social space for people to meet and connect.

In celebrating the rich history of this area we try to look forwards: whether that's through new recompositions of ancient folk tunes, contemporary performances paired with classic films, or through loving repairs to keep the ship alive for another hundred years. Most of all we hope to create a space that feels welcoming - and we can't wait to welcome you onboard!

Our Values


Heritage: We want to celebrate the rich history of the area by opening a public arts centre onboard a living piece of its history.

Diversity: We are committed to developing an arts programme whose range and quality reflect the brilliant diversity of this location and its inhabitants.

Environment: We aim to enhance Canary Wharf’s environment, ecologically and socially, and to serve as a beacon of sustainability.

Community: We hope to enhance the social, cultural and artistic life of the area, by creating a public arts venue which benefits local workers and residents and attracts visitors from across London. We want to remain welcoming and friendly, with a focus on providing shared social space.

Accessibility: This project is committed to accessibility: broadening access to the arts through programming choices and the warmth of our team, removing financial barriers with our no-questions asked discounted tickets policy, and aiming to make our space as physically accessible as we can.


Team


Directors



Click here for more info about Nat & Inigo

Inigo Lapwood

Founding Director

It's no secret that Inigo loves boats. He also loves making and fixing things - ranging from old ship engines, to immersive events, to new language models.

For over ten years Inigo’s work has focussed on the restoration and repair of historic steel ships. He has overseen the full restoration of seven ships, including two on the National Historic Ships register. Consistently delivering marine restoration projects on time and under budget, Inigo is passionately committed to restoring the heritage of our waterways. Inigo is a member of the Council of Experts for National Historic Ships UK, and sits on the London Advisory Board for the Canal and River Trust.

Inigo also works as a creative producer in immersive event production - for the past three years he's been Theatrical Ground Crew Director for Boomtown Festival - the world's largest immersive theatre event.

Additionally, Inigo works as an AI Developer and data-scientist - specialising in natural language analysis. Most recently as lead-developer and a founding director at strategy consultancy R-ai. R-ai takes seriously the idea of listening - talking to every employee in large organisations to help democratise strategic decision making. R-ai has developed an impressive reputation for transforming the effectiveness of large organisations across sectors and across the world. You can read more about Inigo's work at R-ai here.

At Theatreship, Inigo is excited to be bringing these strands of his professional interests together - physically restoring a historic cargo ship, leading on the programming to open the ship up as a public space for innovative events, and grounding the project in active listening to build a project that truly responds to the needs of the people around it. If you see him onboard come say hi!

Nat Hill

Film

When Nat was writing her diary at 5 years old, every page started with 'Today I watched Television'. 40 years later she's a multi-BAFTA winning TV director & producer. Over her 25 year career she's produced some of the most significant shows in Britain, including the Apprentice, 24 hours in A&E, Great British Menu, Stacey Dooley investigates, & Fantastical Food with Heston Blumenthal.

Nat was Creative Director at Rogo films/AJH Media - producers of 'Unprecedented' a ground-breaking documentary with exclusive access to the Trump family, and Grierson shortlisted Bad Boy Chiller Crew.

Most recently she developed and executive produced Netflix documentary series 'The Man with 1000 Kids' exploring the unregulated world of rogue sperm donation. Released last year to critical acclaim the series became Netflix's most viewed show in 95 countries.

Nat brings years of experience in film and TV to her role as head of film programming at Theatreship.

At Theatreship Nat's been critical in developing partnerships with BFI - delivering four BFI funded film festivals to date. She leads the film curation onboard, while managing to be an indispensable part of everything else that happens here too! Expect to see her at our weekly Free Mystery Cinema events where she'll be introducing cinematic gems and sharing what she loves about these films.

You can read more about Nat and some of what she's worked on here.


Curators

More info on our amazing team shortly
(this button currently does nothing!)


Operations


Bar

Right from the start, Theatreship has been designed to be a social space. Part of the joy of coming to live events is seeing them alongside other people, and sharing that experience with the other people onboard. We want everyone to feel welcome here, and no-one to be priced out of enjoying a night onboard, so our bar has the cheapest (and tastiest!) drinks in Canary Wharf.

Menus / prices


If you pop along before 6pm on weekdays, it's our very happy hour, where our organic house wines and craft lager pints can be bought for under a fiver! (a whole 5p under a fiver: £4.95)

One of the pleasures of having an onboard bar is we get to stock the drinks our team love! We've got a particularly nice selection of well-priced single malt whiskeys, some lovely wines, and a rotating selection of cocktails. Ask our team at the bar for their favourites!

Vessel

The Ship then


Built in 1913, the ship was one of the sailing cargo barges that once filled London's docks. Transporting bulk dry cargoes like grain and coal from europe right into the heart of London.


Once a common sight in London's docks, the rise of containerisation in the 1960s moved shipping out of central London and lead to the eventual dereliction of the old docks.

With a riveted steel hull, and classic sweeping lines, the ship speaks to a different age of shipping.

The Ship now


As shipping evolved, so did the ship. With life-extending modifications to her hull and superstructure, she spent over 110 years in continuous service, trading bulk dry cargo around the port cities of Northern Europe.

Now, returning to West India Dock and converted to a performing arts theatre, she continues to serve the needs of the Docklands communities, as she always has.

The Ship in Canary Wharf


The ship has become a new public space, reflecting the rich history of the docks, while looking forwards to a future of live events and lively community.

The ship features a spacious exhibition space on the upper deck, a characterful community café bar on the lower deck, and a 110 seat theatre & cinema space in the old cargo hold. We can't wait to invite you onboard.

Location

Location


The Ship is moored on the Millwall Cutting, London. This is a convenient location, just 30 second walk from the South Quay DLR and a 5 minutes walk from Canary Wharf Jubilee line.

what3words is ///model.potato.works

We are moored on the new Arts and Heritage Berth, alongside other ships of public or historic interest, including Artship and Tugboat Addie, one of only two surviving British Waterways steam tugs.


Volunteer

Get your hands dirty!


The Theatreship project is built on skilled and motivated people coming together and learning from each other. So naturally, skill-sharing is at the heart of what we do. We believe strongly that there should be no barrier to learning new skills, and that no existing skill set or ability prevents you from learning new, unfamiliar ones.

This is why we are always looking for volunteers to get involved with us. Maybe you have particular skills you think could contribute, such as in theatre, production, construction or boat maintenance? Maybe you just want to learn something completely new? We’d love to hear from you!

If you fancy getting involved, then simply click below to sign up and we’ll get back to you.

Ticket prices

Tickets prices may fluctuate at any point. The price paid for a ticket is as offered at the time of purchase and cannot be changed retrospectively. Concessions are only available by booking directly with Regent's Park Open Air Theatre.

Booking Fees and Charges

2026 SEASON

Tickets start at £15, plus £2.50 booking fee per transaction.

One-off events, including takeover days, music and comedy, are priced separately.

MONDAY PRICING

Monday Performances - Tickets for select Monday performances at £35, £25 & £15, plus £2.50 booking fee per transaction.

No concessions available with the exception of access prices.

UNDER 18s

Under 18s save 50%
Valid Tuesday - Thursday evening (and Thursday matinee) performances. Excludes Band AA, Band A & Band F tickets.

U18 tickets can be purchased online. Visit our FAQs for information about bringing children to the Open Air Theatre.

ACCESS

We will offer you the most suitable seat for you and your companion, but will only charge you the cost of the lowest price seat. There are no discounts for shows with a flat price.

No telephone booking fee will be charged on access bookings.

Read more about access

SENIOR CITIZENS

Best available seats at £45, plus £2.50 booking fee per transaction.
Senior Rate midweek matinee tickets can be purchased online.

GRASS BANKS

These tickets are subject to availability on a show by show basis.

Our Grass Banks, to the side of the auditorium, may be available on the day. Whilst we will assess the weather forecast at the time that Grass Bank tickets are released, conditions may change. Therefore, customers should note that they will be seated directly on the ground, which may not be dry. We recommend that you bring a blanket to sit on. Raised seating, such as deckchairs, are not permitted. Tickets will be released at 11am for matinees, and 5pm for evening performances. Tickets can only be purchased in person at the box office, and with a maximum of two tickets per customer.

GROUPS 10+

Save £5 on Price Bands A, B and C. Available on select performances, excluding Monday and Saturday evening.

Discounts can be applied on top of our preview discount.

Groups of 10-19 can be purchased online with no booking fee, or alternatively, over the telephone where a one-off £4.50 telephone transaction fee applies. Groups of 20+ can only be purchased on the telephone. With groups of 20+ the group leader goes free.

Excludes Saturday evenings. Group discount can be combined with preview discount. Discounts and free group leader tickets are only eligible on groups booked within Bands A, B and C.

All discounts and concessions are subject to availability.

Please note, discounts and concessions cannot be combined (unless stated) and are not available retrospectively.

A £2.50 booking fee per transaction applies.

Offering exclusive benefits and discounts, discover more about our Membership and Patron schemes. You can also support the theatre by making a one-off donation.

Funded Tickets

The Unicorn’s doors are open to all children across London and beyond with tickets priced accessibly across the season, with multiple price points. The Creative Hub team work to ensure that the Unicorn is accessible to the children and families who live the closest to us.

Local Funded Tickets
We work with our partner schools and community partners to provide fully funded tickets to local families who might not otherwise have access to the theatre. Please contact creativehub@unicorntheatre.com to find out more.
These tickets are generously supported by the Buffini Chao Foundation and the Hedley Foundation.

School Subsidies
Each year we provide 9,000 fully funded or subsidised tickets to schools who couldn’t otherwise afford a theatre trip for their pupils. For more information about subsidy for schools please contact schools@unicorntheatre.com

Our Subsidised Schools Tickets Programme is generously supported by Sir Harvey and Lady McGrath.

“We can't overstate the difference this makes to our families, particularly our most vulnerable families who are living in extreme poverty, challenging circumstances or who are working with children's services/social care” Loughborough Primary Headteacher

“Since the start of the partnership, one of the biggest changes we’ve seen is in our pupils increased cultural capital- more of our children are regularly going to the theatre.” Hermitage Primary SLT

Wheelchair Tickets

To access these tickets online, log in to your Unicorn Theatre account and select your requirements under Other Preferences. Once these have been selected you will be able to access wheelchair spaces for both Clore and Weston productions. Please note that for allocated performances in the Weston Theatre, you need to select the wheelchair symbol. If you require a complimentary Personal Assistant ticket, please select this option in your Account Preferences; once this information has been updated, you will be able to book this ticket type.

If you have more than two wheelchair users in your group please contact us in advance of the performance date, so we can make sure we hold enough wheelchair spaces for your group.

Wheelchair spaces can also be booked by phone or email, please contact our Box Office team at boxoffice@unicorntheatre.com or on 020 7645 0560.

The Unicorn Theatre is such a fantastic place! Not only is it really accessible which is essential for me in my wheelchair but it’s also so magical too! It’s a wonderful place to visit as a family, from the moment we arrived my little girl was entertained and could interact with the decor in the lobby and the show was just the icing on the cake. If you haven’t already been, then you definitely need to visit!

Sophie Bradbury-Cox (@fashionbelles)

Watch Sophie's video about visiting the Unicorn Theatre with her wheelchair.
